ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. run
   C. happiness
   D. blue

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. went
   C. goes
   D. goed

3. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

4. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

5. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only a joining word
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. No full stops

12. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — run

2. B — went

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

5. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

7. B — Where is the library?

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

10. D — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Word Classes: Adverbs; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 10.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
